questions.question: Why do Go test files use the _test.go suffix?
questions.title: Test File Naming
questions.direct_answer: It makes the file a test file: compiled ONLY by go test (never in the binary). Test functions, helpers, and imports of testing exist only in the test build — zero runtime cost, and the package's public API is the binary's only surface.

sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: It makes the file a test file: compiled ONLY by go test (never in the binary). Test functions, helpers, and imports of testing exist only in the test build — zero runtime cost, and the package's public API is the binary's only surface.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The _test.go suffix does two things:

1. go test finds and compiles the file; go build DOES NOT — the file and everything in it (test functions, test helpers, test-only imports) never ship in the binary.
2. Functions in _test.go files can access the package's INTERNALS (same package) while living outside the production code — white-box testing without polluting the API.

The file-naming conventions:
- `math_test.go` tests math.go (the pairing convention)
- `export_test.go` — the special one: a test-only file that EXPORTS internal functions for external test packages to use (the testing hook pattern)

The package choice: a test file can declare `package math` (same package — access to unexported) or `package math_test` (external — only the public API, testing as a consumer). Both live in the same directory.

The benefit that interviewers want named: the test code is part of the package for DEVELOPMENT (unrestricted access) and absent from the package in PRODUCTION (the _test.go exclusion is absolute). No separate test module, no test-only flags in the binary, no dead test code — the build's binary IS the production code.

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    F[foo_test.go] --> T[go test — compiles]
    F -->|excluded| B[go build — binary]
    PKG1[package math: white-box] --> INT[access unexported]
    PKG2[package math_test: black-box] --> PUB[public API only]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The compilation mechanics: go test builds the package TWICE when there are test files — once for the binary (excluding _test.go), once for the test binary (including them). The test binary imports the testing framework, runs TestMain if present, then the test functions.

The package_test suffix: package math_test is an external test package — it imports math like any consumer would (import "example.com/math"). It sees ONLY the exported identifiers — the black-box test position. The internal package (math, no suffix) sees everything — the white-box position. Both files can test the same code; the choice per test is the access level the test NEEDS.

The export_test.go pattern: the trick for testing internals from external tests — a file with _test suffix in the INTERNAL package that aliases internals to exported names: `var AddInternal = add` — making them visible to math_test consumers for the test build only. The production API stays clean; the test gets access; the naming convention documents the mechanism.
